title: The task leads every screen
statement: Make the task the most prominent thing on each screen, checked on the rendered screen, because a text-pattern check can pass a screen where supporting material buries the task.
example: On one screen, the passage outweighed the learner's task 4:1.
detail: The reading course's quality gates list a passage outweighing the child's task 4:1 among the failures visible only when a screen is rendered and in motion (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/key-quality-gates.md`, line 27). They now require the primary task to win a squint test on blurred screenshots, at least 25% of the viewport on stage screens and no smaller than the largest competitor on work screens, enforced with pixels because a tripwire-only validator once passed a failing screen (the same file, lines 86-89).

evidence.quote: the primary must win the squint test (≥25% viewport on stage screens; ≥ largest competitor on work screens
enforce with pixels, not seam greps: a tripwire-only validator once passed a failing screen).
Both requested four-clue and nested two-clue first arrivals put the current task above the bank; wrong/recovery/quiet controls accepted.
Recovery: 1. remove competing primary controls; 2. collapse earlier material while keeping it accessible; 3. focus the actual new prompt and reduce nonessential decoration.
The audit measured the old 50/50 split giving the passage 28–33% of pixels where the child's act got 5–15% — a 4:1 inversion on the I-do.
